title: Automated Logistics Manifest Verification
business: Logistics and freight companies handling high-volume paper-based shipping documentation.
problem: Manual data entry from scanned shipping manifests is error-prone and creates significant operational bottlenecks during peak transit periods.
solution: Utilize the Qwen3.5-9B image-text-to-text model to ingest scanned manifest images and extract structured data directly into logistics management systems, bypassing manual transcription.
steps: Configure the chat template to support multi-modal input for image processing.
Define a system prompt that instructs the model to identify specific fields like tracking IDs, weight, and destination.
Pass the scanned manifest image along with the text prompt to the model inference endpoint.
Parse the structured output returned by the model to update the internal database.
outcome: Increased throughput of manifest processing and reduced human-in-the-loop verification requirements.
limitation: The model may struggle with low-resolution or heavily skewed scans; verify accuracy by comparing extracted values against checksums or secondary validation fields.
